scope: Intensive second review of exactly the three supplied files. Scores and prior labels were leads only.

samples.marker_note: PHP cache restorer: XOR-hidden command backdoor; relocate traits
execution_and_verdict_evidence: The WordPress init callback checks for a missing local runtime.cache file. A literal Base64 blob decodes to 222 bytes; each byte is XORed with repeating key xmmqhn and written to that missing path.

The recovered 222-byte PHP source is a complete unauthenticated POST command backdoor: proc_open receives the command field as its first argument, stdout is returned with stream_get_contents, then proc_close reaps the process.
The callback overwrites .htaccess with AddHandler application/x-httpd-php .cache, enabling the restored file to execute as PHP where Apache honors the override and handler.
The outer file independently exposes the same POST command process console. There is no authentication, command allowlist or nonexecuting fixture wrapper.

Reconstruction comments disclaim original vendor-plugin/VirusTotal provenance. The executable command endpoints and concealed-extension restoration tip the standalone-machine judgment to MALICIOUS despite possible research use.
limits: WordPress loading/activation, web-root permissions, Apache AllowOverride/handler support and actual deployment authorization are not supplied.
No original compromised plugin, article URL or vendor advisory is present. No family or vendor identity is inferred.
PHP was reviewed statically; only the encoded bytes were decoded and XORed locally. The scanner decodes Base64 but does not automatically recover this repeating-key XOR payload.

samples.marker_note: PHP grouped handler: unauth commands under cache/log PHP handlers
execution_and_verdict_evidence: Loading the file overwrites the local .htaccess with FilesMatch for case-insensitive cache/log extensions and SetHandler application/x-httpd-php.
If POST work is set, its value is passed directly to system; PHP system emits the command output. There is no authentication or command restriction.
The handler setup intentionally permits executable PHP under data/log extensions beside an arbitrary request-driven command endpoint. This tips the standalone-machine judgment to MALICIOUS.
This is explicitly a behavioral reconstruction, not authenticated recovered plugin source. It contains no additional encoded stage or network destination.
limits: Actual web-root placement, Apache support, permissions and operator authorization are unknown. No original compromised package is supplied.

samples.marker_note: MSF-style Next.js scaffold: tool; remove unsupported RCE claims
execution_and_verdict_evidence: The file defines a MetasploitModule subclass, includes the HTTP client mixin, registers target port 3000, and declares a Windows x64 Meterpreter reverse_tcp default payload.

No exploit runs merely from loading the file. When invoked, exploit sends POST /_next/ with Next-Action: x and payload.encoded as the body, ignores the response, then calls execute_command(payload.encoded).

No execute_command implementation or command-stager mixin is supplied. The 694-byte file has no Flight deserialization gadget, child_process invocation, payload downloader, local process execution, persistence or concealed independent stage.

An isolated Ruby trace with framework and HTTP effects mocked confirmed the exact HTTP options and stopped at the missing execute_command method. This verifies local dispatch only, not real Metasploit runtime compatibility or target exploitation.

Explicit framework-shaped, operator-invoked exploit source and disclosed payload configuration tip the judgment to BENIGN offensive tooling. This file is not asserted to be an authentic upstream module or proof of the CVE in its filename.
limits: Actual operator authorization and a deployment environment are unknown. The scaffold is not byte-identical to the upstream React2Shell positive control.
No target was contacted, payload session launched, or CVE validity inferred from the filename.

rule_dispositions.unsupported_claim: Generic MSF inheritance, HTTP use, a Next.js/server-action mention and any payload reference do not establish deserialization, payload transmission or RCE. The provided scaffold is a counterexample.
rule_dispositions.replacement: Preserve source target reference under metadata/lang/source/naming/target. Require actual resolved Flight response prefix/form-data and constructor-path evidence for a hostile Flight aggregate.

rule_dispositions.unsupported_claim: The matcher only requires framework/HTTP/payload/helper-call co-occurrence. The named helper can be unimplemented, and the HTTP call need not transmit it or execute anything.
rule_dispositions.replacement: Existing well-known/tool/offensive/metasploit::http-payload-module retains framework/payload identity. Actual Flight exploit coverage is supplied by the new mechanism rule; other exploit-specific rules remain.

rule_dispositions.change: Move two PHP modulo-XOR loop observations to data/encoding/xor
rule_dispositions.reason: The unchanged loop patterns establish direction-neutral scrambling, not cryptographic encryption. Remove encrypt-specific C0027.001 mapping; preserve notable criticality and every exact consumer.

rule_dispositions.change: Move ten PHP request-command/exception/grouping rules to shell/command-string
rule_dispositions.reason: Command strings are the mechanism; lang was an implementation container. Effective matchers, defaults, exclusions and severities are byte/structure-equivalent. Exact consumers updated; PHP header-backdoor selector retains all formerly selected request atoms.

rule_dispositions.change: Move Rex request call to http/client/exchange and HTTP mixin reference to metadata/import/framework
rule_dispositions.reason: An HTTP exchange and a framework reference are distinct neutral claims. Preserve original matchers and notable criticality. The only ancestor HTTP-lib consumer is Python-scoped, so these Ruby-only observations were ineligible.

rule_dispositions.change: Narrow ATT&CK mappings to supported exploit composites
rule_dispositions.reason: A constructor reference alone does not prove public-service exploitation or JavaScript command execution. The retained fixed Flight shell-gadget composite retains T1190,T1059.007; the new gadget composite claims T1190 only.

coverage_and_disagreements: Both PHP samples retain every accurate pre-review finding after ID normalization, with identical criticalities; cache-restoration has three hostile and three suspicious findings, grouped-handler four hostile and three suspicious findings. Command execution and Apache hidden-data-extension handling are distinct supported hostile patterns across request/command and config.
The Ruby scaffold loses exactly two unsupported hostile aggregates. It retains all accurate HTTP, source-call, payload reference, source-target and MSF identity observations.

An upstream Metasploit Framework 6.4.135 React2Shell module was fetched with forager and inspected. Its real code builds resolved_model response-prefix/form-data objects, constructs constructor property paths, and delivers JavaScript command source via multipart HTTP. The revised mechanism detection retains hostile attack coverage on this external positive; the older fixed constructor/$ACTION_REF_ form remains covered too.

Removal of the generic HTTP exploit fallback can remove generic hostile labels from other modules without mechanism-specific evidence. No unsupported fallback was retained to inflate scores; the retained CouchDB request-binding suite and genuine Flight positives pass.

The classifier still calls grouped-handler BENIGN (level -1) despite four correct hostile traits. This is a preexisting classifier miss; the score is unchanged. cache-restoration stays malicious (level 0), and the Ruby scaffold stays classifier-benign with probability falling from 0.81909674 to 0.03017963.

All three supplied files are plain source with no archive members. No archive member was omitted. The manually recovered PHP stage is a 222-byte command webshell; automatic XOR-payload recovery remains an analyzer limitation, not a reason to omit supported outer-file traits.
Atomscan reports model feature spec v18 versus extractor v19; new-version features are zero-filled. No classifier/model/engine files were edited.
